title: The Drowned Fiddler
text: A fiddler sits on a stump in the marsh, wet through, water running from his hair, playing a jig that will not stop. His fingers are blue. The reeds around him are dancing, as is the mud, and your feet are beginning to tap.

options.label: Dance with the reeds, and let the jig take you.

outcomes.text: You dance a wild hour with mud to the knees, and come away feeling years younger.
You cannot stop; your feet will not obey you. The fiddler smiles with blue lips and plays faster.

options.label: The best talker asks him for a sad song instead, before the dancing takes hold.

outcomes.text: He plays a sad song. The marsh weeps, the reeds lie still and you pass in peace; when you look back, he is still weeping.

options.label: Stop your ears and go round, before your feet betray you.

outcomes.text: The jig follows you for a mile, and your feet keep time with it whether you want them to or not. Everyone is footsore by dark.
